questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the qualifications and conditions of the Governor's office:
1. He must be a citizen of India and have completed the age of 35 years.
2. He must not be a member of either House of Parliament or of a State Legislature.
3. He must belong to the State to which he is appointed.
4. He must not hold any office of profit.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Articles 157 and 158 lay down these conditions; a legislator appointed Governor vacates his seat on the date he enters office. There is no residence rule; appointing an outsider is only a convention, to keep him above local politics.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on the Governor (Art 157, 158)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the tenure of the Governor:
1. He holds office for five years, subject to the pleasure of the President.
2. He continues in office after the expiry of his term until his successor enters upon office.
3. According to the Supreme Court (B. P. Singhal case), a Governor can be removed merely because he differs from the policies of the Union Government.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Article 156 gives a five-year term at the President's pleasure with holdover until the successor takes charge. In B. P. Singhal v. Union of India (2010) the Court held that the pleasure is not unfettered: no reasons need be given, but removal must not be arbitrary or capricious and a policy difference with the Centre is not a valid ground.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on the Governor (Art 156)

questions.q: The oath of office to the Governor of a State is administered by:
o: The Chief Justice of the High Court of the State, or in his absence the senior-most judge of that court
The Speaker of the State Legislative Assembly
questions.e: Article 159 makes the Governor take his oath before the Chief Justice of the High Court of the State, which keeps the Union out of his swearing-in.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on the Governor (Art 159)

questions.q: The provision enabling the same person to be appointed as Governor for two or more States was made by which one of the following?
questions.e: The Seventh Amendment, enacted with the reorganisation of States in 1956, amended the proviso to Article 153. The original Constitution had one Governor per State.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on the Governor (Art 153)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the emoluments of the Governor:
1. They are charged on the Consolidated Fund of the State.
2. They cannot be diminished during his term of office.
3. They are subject to annual vote of the Legislative Assembly.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Charged expenditure is not voted, so the Governor's pay is shielded from the Assembly. Article 158(4) bars its diminution during his term.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on the Governor (Art 158)

questions.q:
The Governor cannot promulgate an ordinance without the previous instructions of the President in which of the following cases?
1. A Bill containing the same provisions would have required the President's previous sanction for its introduction
2. A Bill containing the same provisions would have been reserved for the President's consideration
3. An Act of the State Legislature containing the same provisions would be invalid without the President's assent
4. A Bill on any subject in the State List
Select the correct answer using the code below.
questions.e: Article 213(1) proviso lists exactly three cases where the Union must be taken into confidence. A State List subject is within the State's own competence, so no prior instruction is needed.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on the Governor (Art 213)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the ordinance-making power of the Governor:
1. An ordinance has the same force as an Act of the State Legislature.
2. It can be made only on subjects on which the State Legislature can legislate.
3. It must be approved by Parliament.
4. The Governor can withdraw it at any time.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Under Article 213 an ordinance is laid before the State Legislature; Parliament has no role in approving it. Its scope mirrors the legislature's competence.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on the Governor (Art 213)

questions.q: In which one of the following States does the Governor have a special responsibility with respect to law and order under a provision of the Constitution?
questions.e: Article 371A(1)(b) gives the Nagaland Governor a special responsibility for law and order for as long as internal disturbances in the Naga Hills-Tuensang Area continue; he acts in his individual judgment after consulting the Council of Ministers.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on Special Provisions for Some States (Art 371A)
questions.h: Naga Hills = law and order = Governor's own eyes.

questions.q:
Statement-I: The question whether a matter falls within the Governor's discretion is decided by the Governor himself, and his decision on it is final.
Statement-II: The advice tendered by ministers to the Governor cannot be inquired into by any court.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Article 163(2) makes his decision on whether he is to act in discretion final, and 163(3) bars inquiry into ministerial advice. They are separate protections; neither explains the other.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on the Governor (Art 163)

questions.q: In Rameshwar Prasad v. Union of India (2006), the Supreme Court held that:
o: A Governor's report under Article 356 cannot be examined by any court
The Governor has absolute discretion to dissolve an Assembly without the advice of the Council of Ministers
A Governor can ask a party to prove its majority only in the Raj Bhavan
The dissolution of the Bihar Assembly on the Governor's report was unconstitutional, because the Governor's satisfaction can be examined for mala fides
questions.e: The Court found that the Governor's report in 2005 rested on extraneous material and a speculative claim of horse-trading, so the Presidential proclamation was invalid. It also held that Article 356 is not a tool to keep out a party likely to form a government.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on President's Rule / the Governor

questions.q: In Nabam Rebia v. Deputy Speaker (2016), the Supreme Court held that:
o: The Governor cannot summon, prorogue or dissolve the Assembly in his discretion; he must act on the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers
The Governor may advance the date of the Assembly session on his own discretion
Article 163 gives the Governor a general discretion in all matters where the Constitution is silent
The decisions of a Governor are in no case justiciable
questions.e: The Arunachal Pradesh case limited Article 163: discretion exists only where the Constitution expressly or by necessary implication gives it, and the Article 174 powers are not among them.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on the Governor; Supreme Court, Nabam Rebia (2016)

questions.q: When no party obtains a majority in a State Assembly election, which of the following, according to the Sarkaria Commission, should the Governor invite FIRST to form the government?
o: The single largest party with the support of others, including independents
A post-poll coalition in which all parties join the government
An alliance of parties formed before the election that commands a majority
The leader of a post-poll alliance in which some parties join and others support from outside
questions.e: Sarkaria's order of preference puts the pre-poll alliance first, because voters chose it as a bloc. The single largest party, then a post-poll coalition with all partners in government, then one with outside support, follow.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on the Governor; Sarkaria Commission Report
questions.h: Order: Pre-poll alliance > Largest party > Post-poll all-in > Post-poll outside support.

questions.q: The Constitution requires a Minister in charge of tribal welfare in the Council of Ministers of which one of the following sets of States?
o: Bihar, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh and Odisha
Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Odisha and West Bengal
Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh and Odisha
questions.e: The 94th Amendment (2006) removed Bihar, since the tribal areas went to Jharkhand when the State was split, and added Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand to the proviso to Article 164(1).
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on the State Council of Ministers (Art 164)
questions.h: Tribal-welfare Minister states: CJ-MO (Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, MP, Odisha).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the size of the State Council of Ministers:
1. The total number of ministers, including the Chief Minister, shall not exceed 15 per cent of the total strength of the Legislative Assembly.
2. The number of ministers, including the Chief Minister, shall not be less than 12 in a State.
3. The Council of Ministers of the National Capital Territory of Delhi may have up to 15 per cent of the strength of its Legislative Assembly.
4. The 15 per cent limit is calculated on the strength of the Legislative Council where one exists.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The 91st Amendment (Art 164(1A)) gave the 15 per cent cap and the minimum of 12. Delhi's cap is 10 per cent (Art 239AA(4)), and the cap is always on the Assembly, never the Council.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on the State Council of Ministers; Art 164(1A), 239AA(4)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Article 164 of the Constitution:
1. The Governor appoints all ministers at his own discretion.
2. The ministers hold office during the pleasure of the Governor.
3. The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Legislative Assembly.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Governor appoints the Chief Minister, and the other ministers only on the Chief Minister's advice. Collective responsibility under 164(2) runs to the Assembly, the directly elected House.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on the State Council of Ministers (Art 164)

questions.q:
Under Article 167, the Chief Minister is duty-bound to:
1. Communicate to the Governor all decisions of the Council of Ministers relating to administration and proposals for legislation
2. Furnish such information as the Governor calls for
3. If the Governor so requires, submit for the Council's consideration a matter on which a Minister has taken a decision without Council consideration
Select the correct answer using the code below.
questions.e: Article 167 makes the Chief Minister the channel between Governor and Council, the State counterpart of Article 78 for the Prime Minister.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on the Chief Minister (Art 167)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Chief Minister:
1. He is appointed by the Governor.
2. He must be a member of the Legislative Assembly at the time of his appointment.
3. Other ministers are appointed by the Governor on his advice.
4. His resignation or death dissolves the Council of Ministers.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: A non-member can be appointed CM, but must get elected to the Legislature within six months (Art 164(4)), so statement 2 is wrong. The Council has no existence apart from its head, so his exit dissolves it.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on the Chief Minister

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Article : Provision
1. Article 155 : Appointment of Governor
2. Article 156 : Term of office of Governor
3. Article 157 : Oath or affirmation by Governor
4. Article 162 : Power of Governor to grant pardons
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Article 157 deals with qualifications (oath is Article 159), and pardon is Article 161; Article 162 deals with the extent of the State's executive power.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on the Governor (Art 153-162)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the State Public Service Commission:
1. Its Chairman and members are appointed by the Governor.
2. They can be removed by the Governor on grounds of misbehaviour.
3. For removal on grounds of misbehaviour, the President can act only after a Supreme Court inquiry finds the charge proved.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Under Article 316 the Governor appoints, but only the President can remove, after the Supreme Court reports on a reference; this ties the Commission's security of tenure to the Union and not to the State government of the day.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on State Public Service Commission (Art 316, 317)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Governor's nominating powers in the State Legislature:
1. The Governor nominates one-sixth of the members of the Legislative Council.
2. The nominees are persons with special knowledge or practical experience in literature, science, art, the cooperative movement and social service.
3. Members of the Legislative Council vote in the election of Rajya Sabha members from the State.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Article 171(3)(e) provides the nomination. Rajya Sabha members are elected by the elected members of the Legislative Assembly alone, so MLCs do not vote.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on State Legislature (Art 171)

questions.q: The Governor is required to reserve a Bill passed by the State Legislature for the consideration of the President if, in his opinion, the Bill:
o: Has been returned by him once and passed again by the Legislature
Would so derogate from the powers of the High Court as to endanger the position which the court is designed to fill
Relates to a subject in the Concurrent List
questions.e: This is the only mandatory reservation, under the second proviso to Article 200. All other reservations are discretionary. A re-passed Bill must be assented to by the Governor, who cannot even return a Money Bill.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on the Governor (Art 200)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Bills in a State:
1. The Governor can return a Money Bill to the Legislature for reconsideration.
2. A Bill reserved for the President can be returned by him to the Legislature, which must reconsider it within six months.
3. If the Legislature re-passes such a Bill, the President is not bound to give assent.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Article 200 lets the Governor return only a Bill other than a Money Bill. Under Article 201, unlike Article 111 for Parliament, even a re-passed Bill need not be assented to by the President.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on the Governor (Art 200, 201)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding State finance:
1. The Legislative Council can vote on demands for grants.
2. No demand for a grant can be made except on the recommendation of the Governor.
3. The Contingency Fund of the State is placed at the disposal of the Governor.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Council can only discuss the budget; the Assembly alone votes the grants (Art 203). The Governor holds the Contingency Fund under Article 267(2), parallel to the President's.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on State Legislature / Governor (Art 203, 267)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Governor's address (Articles 175 and 176):
1. The Governor may address either House or both Houses assembled together.
2. He addresses the Legislature at the first session after each general election to the Assembly and at the first session of each year.
3. Where a Legislative Council exists, the Governor's address is delivered only to the Legislative Assembly.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Article 176 requires an address to both Houses assembled together where there are two; the address states the government's policy, just like the President's address.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on State Legislature (Art 175, 176)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Advocate General of a State:
1. He must be qualified to be appointed a judge of a High Court.
2. He is appointed by the Governor.
3. He holds office during the pleasure of the Governor.
4. He receives the remuneration the Governor determines.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: All four are right (Article 165). The Constitution fixes neither his term nor the grounds of removal, so he usually leaves with the government that appointed him.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on the Advocate General (Art 165)

questions.q: Which one of the following is common to the Attorney General for India and the Advocate General of a State?
o: Both are appointed by the President
Both have a right to vote in the legislature in which they speak
Neither has a term fixed by the Constitution
Both are debarred from private legal practice
questions.e: Both hold office during the pleasure of the appointing authority, with the Constitution fixing no term. Each can speak in the legislature but cannot vote, and neither is debarred from private practice.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on Attorney General / Advocate General (Art 76, 165)

questions.q:
Consider the following recommendations regarding Governors:
1. A Governor should belong to the State where he is appointed, so he knows its issues.
2. A Governor should be appointed after effective consultation with the Chief Minister of the State concerned.
3. The five-year tenure of a Governor should not be disturbed except for extremely compelling reasons.
Which of the above were recommended by the Sarkaria Commission?
questions.e: Sarkaria wanted a Governor who is an eminent person from outside the State, detached from local politics, appointed after consulting the Chief Minister, and secure in tenure.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on the Governor; Sarkaria Commission Report

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Punchhi Commission on Centre-State Relations:
1. It recommended that the doctrine of pleasure in respect of the Governor be deleted and that the Governor be removable only by a resolution of the State Legislature.
2. It recommended that the Governor be appointed by the President on the sole advice of the Chief Minister of the State.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Punchhi (2010) recommended removal by a resolution of the State Legislature on the model of impeachment, to protect Governors from arbitrary dismissal. It did not recommend that the Chief Minister alone choose the Governor.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on Centre-State Relations; Punchhi Commission Report

questions.q:
Arrange the following in the chronological order of their appointment:
1. Sarkaria Commission
2. First Administrative Reforms Commission
3. Punchhi Commission
4. National Commission to Review the Working of the Constitution
Select the correct answer using the code below.
questions.e: ARC (1966), Sarkaria (1983), the Venkatachaliah Commission (2000) and Punchhi (2007) each reviewed Centre-State relations.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on Centre-State Relations

questions.q:
Consider the following statements in the context of S. R. Bommai v. Union of India (1994):
1. The Presidential proclamation under Article 356 is wholly immune from judicial review.
2. Whether a ministry has lost the confidence of the House must be tested on the floor of the House.
3. Secularism is a basic feature of the Constitution.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The nine-judge bench made the proclamation reviewable, treated the floor test as the only way to decide majority, and held secularism part of the basic structure.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on President's Rule; S. R. Bommai (1994)

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Case : Holding
1. Hargovind Pant v. Raghukul Tilak : The Governor's office is an independent constitutional office, not an employment under the Government of India
2. B. P. Singhal v. Union of India : A Governor can be removed arbitrarily without any reason
3. Rameshwar Prasad v. Union of India : The Governor's report under Article 356 is immune from judicial review
4. Nabam Rebia v. Deputy Speaker : The Governor can summon the Assembly in his discretion
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Only pair 1 is right. Singhal held removal cannot be arbitrary, Rameshwar Prasad examined the Governor's report, and Nabam Rebia restricted Article 174 to aid and advice.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on the Governor; landmark cases

questions.q: With reference to the Governor's power of pardon under Article 161, which one of the following is correct in light of Epuru Sudhakar v. Government of Andhra Pradesh (2006)?
o: The exercise of the power is open to limited judicial review on grounds such as mala fides or arbitrariness
The exercise of the power is wholly immune from judicial review
The courts can substitute their own view on the merits of the sentence
Only the President's power is open to judicial review, not the Governor's
questions.e: The Court held that the pardon power of the President and Governor is not an act of grace beyond review; the courts can intervene for irrelevant considerations, mala fides or arbitrariness, but cannot sit in appeal.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on the Governor (Art 161); Epuru Sudhakar (2006)

questions.q: The reports of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India relating to the accounts of a State are submitted to:
o: The President, who causes them to be laid before Parliament
The Speaker of the Legislative Assembly
The Governor, who causes them to be laid before the State Legislature
The Chief Minister, who presents them to the Council of Ministers
questions.e: Article 151(2) says that State audit reports go to the Governor. This is why the Public Accounts Committee of the State scrutinises them after the Governor places them before the Legislature.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on CAG (Art 151)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding local-body institutions:
1. The State Election Commissioner is appointed by the Governor.
2. The Governor can remove the State Election Commissioner at his pleasure.
3. The State Finance Commission is constituted by the Governor every five years.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Article 243K gives the Commissioner security: he can be removed only as a High Court judge is. The Finance Commission under Article 243-I reviews the finances of Panchayats and Municipalities every five years.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapters on Panchayati Raj and Municipalities (Art 243K, 243-I)

questions.q: The system of appointing the Governor by the Union executive was borrowed from the Constitution of:
questions.e: The Draft Constitution had an elected Governor, but the Constituent Assembly chose the Canadian model of an appointee of the Centre. The USA elects Governors directly.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on Sources of the Constitution / Governor

questions.q: Who was the first woman to hold the office of Governor of a State in independent India?
questions.e: Sarojini Naidu was Governor of the United Provinces (now Uttar Pradesh) from 1947 to 1949. Padmaja Naidu followed in West Bengal, and Vijaya Lakshmi Pandit in Maharashtra.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on the Governor; list of Governors

questions.q: In S. R. Chaudhuri v. State of Punjab (2001), the Supreme Court held that:
o: A non-legislator can be appointed minister repeatedly for successive six-month periods
A Chief Minister must be a member of the Legislative Assembly at the time of appointment
A minister who is not a legislator can continue for one year before he must be elected
A person who is not a legislator cannot be reappointed minister for a fresh six-month period without being elected to the Legislature
questions.e: Article 164(4) lets a non-member serve for six months; allowing repeated reappointment would defeat the rule that ministers must be answerable to the legislature.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on the State Council of Ministers (Art 164(4)); S. R. Chaudhuri (2001)

questions.q:
In which of the following matters does the Governor act in his discretion?
1. Reserving a Bill for the consideration of the President
2. Recommending President's Rule in the State
3. Appointing the Chief Minister when no party has a clear majority
4. Granting assent to an ordinary Bill duly passed by the Legislature on the advice of the ministers
Select the correct answer using the code below.
questions.e: These three are the standard discretionary acts. Assent to a Bill that the government supports is given on ministerial advice.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on the Governor (discretionary powers)

questions.q:
Statement-I: The office of the Governor is an independent constitutional office and not an employment under the Government of India.
Statement-II: The Governor can be removed by the President only on the ground of proved misbehaviour.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: The first is the holding in Hargovind Pant. The second is false: Article 156 gives the President a pleasure power, and no misbehaviour inquiry is required.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on the Governor (Art 156)

questions.q:
Statement-I: A Governor cannot return a Money Bill to the State Legislature for reconsideration.
Statement-II: A Money Bill can be introduced in the Legislative Assembly only on the recommendation of the Governor.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Article 200 allows return of only a Bill 'other than a Money Bill'. Article 207 requires the Governor's recommendation to introduce one. Both are correct but unconnected.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on State Legislature (Art 200, 207)

questions.q:
Statement-I: A Chief Minister who has lost the confidence of the Legislative Assembly must resign or advise dissolution.
Statement-II: The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Legislative Assembly.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Article 164(2) makes the Council collectively responsible to the Assembly, so loss of its confidence ends the Council's mandate, and the CM must resign or seek dissolution.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on the State Council of Ministers (Art 164(2))

questions.q:
Match List-I (Article of the Constitution) with List-II (State) and select the correct answer:
List-I: A. Article 371A  B. Article 371G  C. Article 371H  D. Article 371J
List-II: 1. Karnataka  2. Mizoram  3. Nagaland  4. Arunachal Pradesh
questions.e: 371A is Nagaland, 371G is Mizoram, 371H is Arunachal Pradesh, and 371J (98th Amendment) deals with the Hyderabad-Karnataka region.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on Special Provisions for Some States

questions.q:
Match List-I (Article) with List-II (Provision):
List-I: A. Article 161  B. Article 165  C. Article 213  D. Article 174
List-II: 1. Advocate General  2. Power to promulgate ordinances  3. Power to grant pardons  4. Sessions, prorogation and dissolution
questions.e: The matching is a straight recall of the Governor's four main areas: judicial, law officer, legislative and summoning powers.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on the Governor (Art 161, 165, 213, 174)

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT appointed by the Governor of a State?
o: The Chairman of the State Public Service Commission
questions.e: High Court judges are appointed by the President after consultation with the Chief Justice of India, the Governor and the Chief Justice of the High Court (Art 217).
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on the Governor; chapter on High Court (Art 217)

questions.q: District judges in a State are appointed by:
o: The Chief Justice of the High Court alone
The Governor, in consultation with the High Court
The President, in consultation with the Chief Justice of India
questions.e: Under Article 233 the Governor appoints, posts and promotes district judges after consulting the High Court; the High Court then controls subordinate courts under Article 235.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on Subordinate Courts (Art 233)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Governor's powers in respect of the State Legislature:
1. He can summon each House of the State Legislature.
2. He can prorogue the Houses.
3. He can dissolve the Legislative Council.
4. He can dissolve the Legislative Assembly.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Legislative Council, like the Rajya Sabha, is a permanent House that is not subject to dissolution; one-third of its members retire every second year.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on State Legislature (Art 174)

questions.q: The pro-tem Speaker of a newly elected State Legislative Assembly is appointed by:
o: The Chief Justice of the High Court
questions.e: The Speaker vacates office just before the first meeting of the new Assembly, and the Governor appoints a pro-tem Speaker to administer the oath to members and conduct the election of the new Speaker.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on State Legislature

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Article 166:
1. All executive action of the State Government is expressed to be taken in the name of the Governor.
2. The Governor makes rules for the more convenient transaction of the business of the State Government and its allocation among ministers.
3. The Governor requires the prior approval of the Union Government to make such rules.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Article 166 is the State counterpart of Article 77. Nothing in it requires the Union's approval.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on the Governor (Art 166)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the life of a Governor's ordinance:
1. It ceases to operate at the expiration of six weeks from the reassembly of the Legislature unless disapproved earlier.
2. If the two Houses reassemble on different dates, the six weeks are counted from the later date.
3. A resolution of the Legislative Assembly alone is enough to disapprove it even where a Legislative Council exists.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Article 213(2) requires that the disapproving Assembly resolution be agreed to by the Council where one exists, so statement 3 is wrong. The later-date rule for the six weeks is in the same clause.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on the Governor (Art 213)

questions.q: The duty of the Union to protect every State against external aggression and internal disturbance, and to ensure that the government of every State is carried on in accordance with the Constitution, is contained in:
questions.e: Article 355 states the duty; Article 356 is the means used when a State's constitutional machinery fails.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on Emergency Provisions (Art 355)
